findings: The initial namespace error was corrected through teacher feedback; sources and m17 were successfully acquired.
On the acquired register cut Qwen identified 8,12,16 in its understanding, yet requested the already selected complete m17 as a full version.
Two native admission rejections explicitly required a repeat reason or revised action. The returned raw content was identical twice, with repeat_reason null.
C0 did not execute either rejected duplicate read. It stopped on the frozen correction bound.
The failed draft stopped inquiry 2 before its teacher critique; this run therefore does not establish that an intensive teacher could not correct that draft.
Typed justification and prompt compaction improve observability and mechanical protection but do not demonstrate reliable evidence-to-action reasoning.
No interview, capture notebook or final submission occurred. No weights changed, transfer or comparative benefit was shown.
Reopening retained the same native snapshot without new dispatches. This is a normal terminal reopen, not cross-owner crash recovery qualification.
next_engineering_question: How should rejected draft decisions reach fallible teacher review before correction exhaustion while only admitted revisions can execute? Diagnose that orchestration boundary before any further identical live run.
